mission_instrument: Apollo 15 (July and August 1971), onboard ECG biotelemetry as described in Biomedical Results of Apollo, Section II Chapter 1
preprocessing: Events transcribed by hand from the chapter text with verbatim sentences (OCR word spacing restored). 'about 179:05' is 179:07 minus the printed one and one-half minutes. No value read from the ECG tracing figure.
license_terms: NASA publication, public domain in the United States
provenance: REPLAY. Event descriptions and approximate heart rates printed in a NASA book; not ECG samples.
is_not: Not an ECG waveform or a heart rate series. Not the in-flight potassium level: potassium was measured only postflight.

consumers.use: Pulse and ECG device twins: a pulse number alone cannot show bigeminy; the rhythm family needs an ECG
Kit change after the event: antiarrhythmics added for Apollo 16
Eval scenario: unexplained extreme fatigue during heavy work, rhythm unknown to the crewman
